visuals.title: Who keeps pH steady
visuals.text: Lungs adjust CO2 in minutes; kidneys adjust bicarbonate and H+ excretion over days; blood buffers instantly.

glossary.pH: A measure of how acidic the blood is; lower numbers mean more acid.
glossary.Respiratory: Here, an acid-base change driven by CO2 and breathing.
glossary.Metabolic: Here, an acid-base change driven by bicarbonate or non-CO2 acids.
glossary.Non-specific: Not pointing to any one particular diagnosis.
glossary.Compensated: The opposite system has adjusted enough to bring pH back to normal.
glossary.Na: Sodium, the main positive ion in blood.
glossary.Cl: Chloride, a main negative ion in blood.
glossary.Ketones: Acids made from fat breakdown when insulin is lacking, as in DKA.
glossary.Paracetamol: A common painkiller; overdose can contribute to a raised anion gap acidosis.
glossary.Propylene glycol: A solvent in some IV drugs that can build up and cause acidosis.
glossary.Isoniazid: An anti-tuberculosis antibiotic that can cause seizures and lactic acidosis in overdose.
glossary.AKI: Acute kidney injury: a sudden fall in kidney function.
glossary.Sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.Mesenteric ischaemia: Loss of blood supply to the bowel, producing lactate.
glossary.Crohn's: Crohn's disease: a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can cause diarrhoea.
glossary.Partial respiratory compensation: Breathing changes that move pH back towards normal but not fully.
glossary.Secretory: Producing fluid; a secretory villous adenoma leaks salt-rich mucus into the bowel.
glossary.Decreased PaCO2: Lower than normal carbon dioxide in arterial blood, from overbreathing.
glossary.Panic attacks: Sudden episodes of intense fear with fast breathing and palpitations.
glossary.Hypocalcaemia: Low blood calcium; overbreathing lowers ionised calcium, causing tingling and cramps.
glossary.Aspirin overdose: Salicylate poisoning; early on it stimulates breathing, later causes metabolic acidosis.
glossary.PE: Pulmonary embolism: a clot blocking an artery in the lungs.
glossary.High altitude: Low oxygen at height drives overbreathing and respiratory alkalosis.
glossary.Chronic bronchitis: Long-term productive cough from inflamed airways, part of COPD.
glossary.Mucus hypersecretion: Overproduction of mucus by the airways.
glossary.Heroin: An opioid drug; overdose slows breathing.
glossary.Overdose: Taking more of a drug than is safe.
glossary.Arterial blood gas: A blood sample from an artery measuring pH, oxygen, CO2 and bicarbonate.
glossary.Targeted blood tests: Tests chosen to look for a suspected cause, such as ketones or lactate.
glossary.Insulin: The hormone that lets cells take up glucose and switches off ketone production.
glossary.Controlled oxygen: Oxygen given at a set, limited dose to avoid worsening CO2 retention.
glossary.Antibiotics: Drugs that kill or stop the growth of bacteria.
glossary.IV fluids: Fluids given directly into a vein.
glossary.Antidote: A drug that reverses the effect of a poison.
glossary.Decontamination: Removing or binding a poison so less is absorbed.
glossary.Alkalinise urine: Make the urine less acidic so more salicylate is trapped and excreted.
glossary.Elimination: Removal of a drug or toxin from the body.
glossary.Rebreathing mask: A mask that lets the patient breathe back exhaled CO2 to correct overbreathing.
glossary.Supportive care: Treatment that maintains body functions while the cause is treated.
glossary.Ventilation: Mechanical breathing support from a machine.
glossary.Hydrogen ion: H+, the particle that makes a solution acidic.
glossary.Excretion: Removal of waste from the body, here by the kidneys into urine.
glossary.Volatile acid: An acid that can be breathed out as a gas; carbonic acid leaves as CO2.
glossary.Lactate: An acid produced when tissues lack oxygen.
glossary.Alveolar hypoventilation: Too little air reaching the alveoli, so CO2 builds up.
glossary.CO2 retention: Build-up of carbon dioxide in the blood.
glossary.Opioid: A class of strong painkillers, including morphine and heroin, that slow breathing.
glossary.Neuromuscular weakness: Weak breathing muscles from nerve or muscle disease.
glossary.Alveolar hyperventilation: Too much air moving through the alveoli, blowing off CO2.
glossary.Hydrochloric acid: HCl, the acid made by the stomach lining.
glossary.Volume depletion: Loss of fluid from the body's circulation.
glossary.Carbonic acid: H2CO3, formed when CO2 dissolves in water; splits into H+ and bicarbonate.
